chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi and al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'How many people have a right (of inheritance) that they do not know about?' I said: 'And what is that, may Allah rectify you?' He said: 'Indeed, two neighbors had a treasure beneath them that they did not know about. Know that it was not gold nor silver.' I said: 'Then what was it?' He said: 'It was knowledge.' I said: 'Which of the two is more entitled to it?' He said: 'The elder.' Thus we say.'

key_terms.حَقٌّ: Right (specifically inheritance right in this context)
key_terms.صَاحِبَيِ الْجِدَارِ: The two neighbors (literally: the two owners of the wall)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith about the two neighbors and the hidden treasure of knowledge?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a hidden treasure of 'knowledge' beneath two walls to illustrate that inheritance rights can extend beyond material wealth to include spiritual or intellectual legacy. The Imam clarifies that this is not gold or silver, but rather 'ilm' (knowledge), establishing a principle where seniority (the elder) holds priority in inheriting such rights. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that knowledge is a tangible asset of inheritance, often overlooked in favor of material distribution, and highlights the importance of recognizing non-material entitlements within the family structure.
